Official

uh-FISH-uhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Official is approved by an authority; formal and proper.

The official school calendar says winter break starts Friday.

Worked Example

The race results are not official until the judges check every time.

The results only count after the judges - the people in charge - approve them. Official means approved by an authority.

How Official Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

approved

approved: given a yes by someone in charge

authorized

authorized: given permission by an authority

Antonyms

unofficial

unofficial: not approved by anyone in charge

unauthorized

unauthorized: done without permission

How Strong Is It? — Allowed → official → Legal

Allowed vs. official

Allowed vs. official: Allowed is milder: sneakers are allowed at recess, but no one signed a paper about it.

Legal vs. official

Legal vs. official: Legal is stronger: a legal rule is backed by the government itself.

Put it together

Put it together: Offici- means duty or job, so official describes things approved by the people whose job it is to decide.
